historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Freelander 3.2 i6 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 3.2 i6 variant launched in the Freelander 2 (L359) range, it brought Volvo-sourced inline-six petrol performance to the compact SUV lineup, offering smooth power delivery and strong towing capability. This engine remained the flagship petrol option throughout the Freelander 2 production run.

milestones.description: B6324S, 3.2L Inline-6 Petrol, 230 PS (Introduction of the 3.2 i6 powertrain to the Freelander 2 L359 range, featuring Volvo's proven inline-six architecture with variable valve timing).
B6324S (updated), 3.2L Inline-6 Petrol, 230 PS (Minor calibration updates and emissions compliance improvements, maintaining the same core engine architecture).
End of production (Freelander 2 discontinued, replaced by Discovery Sport with Ingenium engines).

problems.group: Timing Chain Tensioner & Cooling System Failures
problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner & Cooling System Failures - Why the Land Rover Freelander 3.2 i6 B6324S Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: Timing chain tensioner wear can lead to chain stretch and rattling noises, while water pump failure and coolant leaks from crossover pipes are common age-related issues on this Volvo-sourced inline-six.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing the water pump, inspecting timing chain tensioners, and addressing coolant leaks.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for early-stage symptoms; prevents catastrophic timing failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if the engine has suffered catastrophic timing failure or block damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Freelander 3.2 i6 (L359) is worth £3,000-£9,000+ `[THIRD-PARTY]`. At this value range, a rebuilt engine replacement cost can represent 50-80% of the vehicle's value on lower-value examples, making careful evaluation essential. On well-maintained, higher-value examples, replacement remains viable.
problems.recommendation: If the issue is strictly early-stage cooling system related, a specialist water pump replacement and coolant system overhaul is the most cost-effective fix. However, if there is accompanying timing chain rattle, loss of compression, or internal damage, a fully rebuilt unit with all known vulnerabilities addressed is the safest long-term choice. For sub-£5,000 Freelander 3.2 i6 examples, carefully evaluate whether replacement cost justifies the investment versus part-exchange or scrap value.
